columns.title: Ideation and concept development
columns.summary: Find the experience you want to offer, explore several concepts, and write the X.
work: Start from a player motivation and treat it as a hypothesis tied to behavior you can observe.
Explore two or three concepts before committing; genre sets expectations and production demands.
Study specific moments in reference games; record attribution and reuse terms.
Write the X: one sentence that states the game.
investigate: Which player motivation are you offering, stated as behavior you could observe?
Which two or three concepts did you compare, and why does one win?
What do specific moments in reference games teach you, and on what reuse terms?

columns.title: G1 Concept
columns.question: Is this idea sufficiently clear and achievable to justify prototype work?
work: Define the player, experience, core loop, references, and boundaries.
Name the largest design and technical uncertainties.
Decide what the in-game agent contributes and what a scripted baseline does.
Estimate time, model latency, and cost.
evidence: X, core loop, references and attribution, systems diagram
Initial project plan (any format), Initial GDD, and Configuration Document
AI design hypothesis, scripted baseline, playtest question, latency and cost budgets

critical.opportunity: What experience are you offering, to which player, and why is it worth pursuing?
critical.execution: What core loop, agent role, and scripted baseline will the prototype test, and how?
critical.risks: What are the largest design and technical uncertainties, how will you detect them, and what will you do?
critical.alignment: Do the pitch, Initial GDD, Configuration Document, and plan describe the same game?

also: What would the player lose if the agent were replaced by the scripted baseline?
What are the latency and cost budgets, and what are they based on?
What is in scope, what is excluded, and what would you reduce first?

columns.title: Prototyping and player observation
columns.summary: Build the core interaction and the bounded agent, then watch an external player use it.
work: Implement the core interaction and bounded agent behavior.
Run deterministic checks and budgeted live evaluation.
Observe an external player using the loop.
Keep what happened apart from your explanation of why.
investigate: Does an external player use the core loop the way you intended?
Does the agent help the player without revealing what it should not know?
What happened, kept separate from why you think it happened?

columns.title: G2 Prototype
columns.when: Mon Nov 30, with G3 (recording Sat Nov 28)
columns.question: What evidence supports the core experience, including the agent's contribution?
work: Show the first playable with its agent.
Show what an external player did with the core loop.
Separate findings that need design changes from findings that need code changes.

critical.opportunity: Did observed players get the experience you intended?
critical.execution: What does the first playable demonstrate, including the agent's contribution?
critical.risks: Which assumptions failed, which failures can you reproduce, and what did you change?
critical.alignment: Does the agent's configured knowledge match the GDD's information boundaries?

also: Which findings need a design change, and which need a code change?
What does the evidence not yet support?

columns.title: Production planning and feasibility checks
columns.when: Nov 16 to Nov 28, alongside the prototype
columns.summary: Turn the demonstrated experience into a plan you can finish, with Alpha, Beta, and Gold checks.
work: Identify dependencies, asset and content work, role coverage, tests, and release preparation.
Define Alpha, Beta, and Gold acceptance checks.
Decide what stays, what is excluded, and what can shrink.
Give every fallback a trigger and a concrete action.
investigate: What work remains, at what quality, and what depends on what?
Which roles in your agent team cover that work, and where are the gaps?
What gets cut first, and what triggers each fallback?

columns.title: G3 Production
columns.question: Can you complete the agreed game with the time and resources remaining?
work: Propose the scope lock and the exclusions list.
Show capacity, dependencies, and contingencies.

critical.opportunity: Is the demonstrated experience still worth the time that remains?
critical.execution: Can you finish the agreed scope with your remaining time and capacity, including release testing?
critical.risks: What is excluded, what shrinks first, and what triggers each fallback?
critical.alignment: Do the scope-lock plan, GDD, and agent team coverage describe the same game?

also: What are the Alpha, Beta, and Gold acceptance checks?
Where is the buffer for a release playtest and fixes?

columns.title: Production, integration, testing, and release preparation
columns.summary: Reach Alpha, lock content at Beta, run a release playtest, and verify fixes.
work: Alpha: all agreed features integrated well enough to exercise.
Beta: release content complete and locked; work turns to fixes and polish.
Observe an external release playtest after Alpha and before the Gold recording.
Classify problems by consequence; name build, steps, owner, and verification.
investigate: Are all agreed features integrated well enough to exercise (Alpha)?
Is release content complete and locked (Beta)?
Did an external release playtest change anything, and do the fixes hold?

columns.title: G4 Final / Pre-Launch Review
columns.question: Is this identified build ready for release or showcase?
work: Identify the exact Gold candidate and its configuration.
Show triaged fixes verified and accepted defects listed.
Show full development-role coverage.
evidence: Update Playtest Log and Risk Register
Release instructions another person can follow

critical.opportunity: Does this build deliver the X to its intended players?
critical.execution: Which exact build is ready, and what release checks and verified fixes show it?
critical.risks: Which defects do you accept and why, and what is the deterministic fallback?
critical.alignment: Do the Final GDD, Configuration Document, and build agree, with every role covered?

also: Can another person run the release from its instructions alone?
Which model and configuration were tested, including failed runs?

columns.title: Release, showcase, feedback, and reflection
columns.summary: Release the Gold build, collect feedback, play three classmates' builds, and draft the AAR.
work: Release or showcase the approved game.
Collect feedback and complete the Playtest Log.
Play the three assigned classmates' builds.
Review decisions, failures, changes, and agent handoffs.
investigate: Can players reach and run the released game?
What did players and classmates report?
How does the result compare with what you set out to make?

columns.title: G5 Retrospective / Closure
columns.question: What does the finished project teach, and can someone understand and use its archive?
work: Compare the result with the original intentions.
Account for the full agent team and the decisions you kept.

critical.opportunity: What did players experience compared with what you intended?
critical.execution: What did the process deliver, what slipped, and why?
critical.risks: Which risks happened, and did your responses work?
critical.alignment: Can someone find the approved build and the evidence behind the AAR's conclusions?

also: Which decisions did you keep as Executive Producer and Creative Director?
What would you test first in a next version?
